title: V1-a — The spare liner in the handbag (handbag-cam, post-sneeze) · Angle A2 "Not a pad, not a diaper" · impersonal brand VO over b-roll · undated "Sneeze. Little pee." open · 35s cold TOF (55s long cut)

goal_target.avatar_line: The Pad-and-Liner Mom (quiz persona 'The Comeback'): a woman 30-45, core mid-30s (ICP 'Mara, 36'; #14 'I'm 37 and have two kids'), back to moving after kids, who pees a little on a hard sneeze, a big laugh or a jump and gets by with a panty liner 'just in case', peeing before she leaves and crossing her legs. Strong, capable, private (#4 'except my husband and mom'), wry resignation; 'diaper' and 'old' repel her. Problem-aware, not yet burned (hasn't bought). We write to ONE of her: the woman who just sneezed in a car park and reached for the spare liner.
goal_target.core_desire_why_chain: Surface: 'I want underwear that handles the sneeze so I can stop carrying a liner.' -> why? 'So I'm not planning my errands/class around a leak and a spare.' -> why? 'So I can move, laugh and sneeze without bracing or crossing my legs.' -> why? 'So this stops being a daily chore that reminds me something's wrong.' -> DEEP DRIVER (Doc 3 §16): 'So I'm still ME - strong, capable, not falling apart, not old.' We write to the core: sell back the ease and the self-image, not a dry gusset.
goal_target.angle: A2 - Not a pad, not a diaper. The ONE problem attacked = the liner/pad workaround itself: a sticker that bunches, shifts, feels like a diaper and goes in the trash every single day - vs plain black briefs you just pull on. NOT the leak mechanism (banned on CJ), NOT 'period products can't hold urine' (banned). Contrast is form + routine only.
goal_target.emotion: Validated relief + dry, athlete-to-athlete humour about pee. Valence positive/wry; intensity low-to-moderate. The live spark is a small eye-roll at the daily sticker routine (anger at the hassle and at being sold a sticker - Doc 2/3 anger 20 > shame 11, aimed at the category, never herself), resolving into the relief of 'oh - it could just be underwear.' Never shame, never fear, never 'embarrassing' (also Meta appearance-inferiority safe).

dials.awareness_and_entry: Problem-aware, single level, no mixing. She knows she leaks and names the moment; she does NOT know underwear is made for it, so she improvises with a liner 'just in case'. ENTER on the object + moment: a POV inside her handbag the instant after a sneeze, as her hand grabs the spare liner, with the undated moment line 'Sneeze. Little pee.' burned in at 0.0s and a lightly-agitated repetition question ('Still packing a spare liner?'). Never 'Do you leak?', never a condition question, never 'why is it the wrong tool' (adequacy framing is banned on CJ).
dials.sophistication_and_positioning: Stage 4-5, ~1/3 burned (Doc 1 §8). Loud players sell age-identity ('over 60') and bigger mechanism claims; on CJ we can run NEITHER mechanism nor an out-claim. So enter on EXPERIENCE + Stage-5 NEW-CATEGORY identity: 'it's just underwear - not a pad, not a diaper', the active everyday woman's category. Positioning = plain black briefs she recognises as normal underwear, pulled on. Proof deferred to the 30-Night Leak-Test, not asserted in-ad.
dials.funnel_move: From a scrolling cold stranger -> a QUALIFIED click into the quiz 'Find my match'. Qualified = by the end she knows this is leak-resistant underwear for the sneeze and that she's clicking to a quiz that finds her size and how many pairs. No curiosity-bait.
dials.modifiers: (1) Belief-change depth = skepticism x price: TOF, NO price shown, so the in-ad belief lift is small ('there's underwear made for this + a risk-free way to test it'); heavy proof deferred to the quiz+offer; the guarantee line does the trust work. (2) Identity depth: identity-linked buy (strong/not-old) -> touch identity lightly ('just underwear', an active everyday woman who moves on unbothered), don't go deep in 35s. (3) Length/arc: 35s > 20s, so build a light arc (hook -> the liner's day -> the 'or...' reveal -> resolve+CTA) with one small open loop (a 0.4s brief pre-tease paid off at the 'Or...' turn); the 55s cut adds the care beat + a second everyday movement.
dials.what_this_ad_must_do: Stop the scroll on the liner dominating frame 1 + the post-sneeze grab; name the moment + the word pee in BOTH sound-off and sound-on by ~0.5s; reframe the daily-liner workaround as the real problem (A2, form/routine only); reveal plain black briefs as the category (pull on, go) by ~11s; de-risk in one line (30 nights to see if they hold, money back if they don't); hand a qualified click to the quiz. Earn the click, not the sale.

pulled.format: V1 - Problem object + impersonal brand voiceover over b-roll. A clean, unbranded white panty liner is the hook; the plain black CJ brief is the payoff; a warm, wry impersonal brand narrator (never I/we, never 'you leak') carries the VO, recorded first with the pictures cut to it.
pulled.hook_format: Object-cam POV (handbag-cam) + undated moment line burned in from frame 1, the VO mirroring it word-for-word so sound-on and sound-off get the same hook AND the same word 'pee'. Then a repetition question (not an adequacy question) and the proven problem-object-to-product reveal under the impersonal VO.
pulled.structure: Beat skeleton, two cuts (35s main / 55s long test). The separate silent 3-6s setup beat is DROPPED (plan line 670): the TEASE bridge is folded into the VO lead-in and we hard-cut from the hook straight into the self-roast with burned-in text throughout. 0.0-1.4s HOOK (handbag-cam: liner dominant 40%+ of frame, 'Sneeze. Little pee.' burned in at 0.0s, ACHOO jolt + the grab); 1.4-3.0s HOOK pt2 (repetition question 'Still packing a spare liner?'); 3.0-11.0s LINER SELF-ROAST (bridge lead-in VO + CJ attributes only: bunches, shifts, feels like a diaper, another one in the trash by tonight, a fresh one tomorrow) with a 0.4s brief pre-tease flash '...or this.' at ~8.5s; 11.0-23.0s REVEAL (plain black brief stretched in hand, AI woman pulling leggings over it, one everyday capability movement); 23.0-30.0s RESOLVE + qualified CTA ('Not a pad. Not a diaper. Take the quiz - it finds your size and how many pairs'); 30.0-35.0s END CARD (guarantee + money-back + 'Find my match'). No price, gifts, 'new', stats, mechanism, reviews or dated line.
pulled.visual_hook: Miro #75 'Fridge POV' shot as a handbag-cam. Why: the camera sits where the product lives (inside the unzipped bag) and the hand lunges for the liner - a viewpoint nobody has seen in a feed of faces, with the enemy object (the liner) DOMINATING frame 1 (fills 40%+, keys/phone thrown out of focus so the category reads instantly) and the sneeze happening BEFORE the grab, so it reads as the real post-sneeze spare-liner swap liner-users know, not an impossible pre-sneeze fix. In-category twin: Everdries 1206351388295667 (275d, video#14), POV down at the object with a line burned in from frame 1.

fundamentals.authority_facts: No doctor, no stat (none allowed in round-1). Authority = plain TRUE facts stated flat, which is new specific info the viewer hasn't seen framed this way: the liner's actual daily routine ('It bunches. It shifts. It feels like a diaper. Another one in the trash by tonight. Tomorrow, a new one.') and the plain product/guarantee fact on the end card ('30 nights to see if they hold - money back if they don't'). Telling the honest truth about the object IS the authority - no claim needed.
fundamentals.positioning: Matches Stage 5 new-category/identity: 'just underwear - not a pad, not a diaper', the active everyday woman's category. Shown, not said: a plain black brief pulled on like normal underwear, worn by a real-looking 30-45 woman who gets on with an everyday errand, relaxed and in control.
fundamentals.speed_to_value: Value signalled by ~0.5s in BOTH modes: 'Sneeze. Little pee.' burned in at 0.0s with the liner filling 40%+ of frame 1 (sound-off), and the VO 'Sneeze. Little pee.' from 0.1s (sound-on). The moment is named with the word pee - on screen AND spoken - before the first half-second is out. No dated line burns the opening real estate.
fundamentals.clarity_grade: 5th-8th grade, active voice, one idea per line. VO is short staccato sentences ('It bunches. It shifts. It feels like a diaper.'). No clinical words, her vocabulary only.
fundamentals.value_lens_ease: Hormozi value = (dream x likelihood) / (time x effort). Lead with EASE: 'Pull them on, and go about the day' - nothing to stick, pack or swap; set directly against the daily sticker routine (buy it, stick it, it bunches, bin it, repeat). The effort side of the enemy is shown; the ease of the cure is shown.
fundamentals.delivery: Staccato, varied pace; forced-up wry energy; crystal enunciation; hook on-screen AND in VO (now truly mirrored). SHOW the contrast (liner bunching/going in the trash vs the brief pulled on and walking off). Cuts match the staccato: one continuous hook shot through 1.4s (no cut in the first 1.2s per plan), hard cut out of the bag at ~2.2s, quick 1-1.5s liner b-roll cuts on the beat, a 0.4s brief flash at ~8.5s, one clean reveal push.
fundamentals.emotional_resonance: Validated relief + dry humour: the eye-roll at 'same sticker, same routine', the lift at 'Or... it could just be underwear.' Carries the anger-at-the-hassle (not herself) and resolves to ease and quiet capability (she moves on unbothered). No shame, no fear, no 'embarrassing'.
fundamentals.human_voice: Her words, matter-of-fact, athlete-to-athlete: 'a big sneeze, a little pee', 'just pull them on'. Sounds like a wry friend, not a brand. Borrowed from #19 ('pee a tiny bit... every time I... sneezed'), #34 ('peeing a little every time i sneeze'), #119 ('sick and tired of peeing myself every time I sneeze'), #30 (the pre-planned 'just in case' habit). 'pee' is brand-approved (the live hero is 'I'll pee myself').
fundamentals.honesty_flaw_flip: Raise the honest limit and flip it: we make NO claim that it holds - instead the locked guarantee, verbatim: 'Wear them through your moment for 30 nights. If they don't hold, you get your money back.' The underdog honesty (test it on your own sneeze) IS the brand (Doc 4 §4B 'we out-honest them'). No fake proof anywhere.

primary_text:
Keys, phone, spare liner.

A big sneeze, a little pee - and so far the plan's a sticker that bunches, shifts, feels like a diaper, and lands in the trash by tonight. Then tomorrow, a new one.

There's a less sticky plan: plain black briefs you just pull on. Not a pad. Not a diaper.

Take the quiz and find your match. Wear them through your moment for 30 nights. If they don't hold, you get your money back.

Find my match >

Made with AI. Product images based on the real brief.
headline: Not a pad. Not a diaper. Just underwear.
cta: One CTA, to the quiz: "Find my match" (VO hardened: "Take the quiz - it finds your size and how many pairs"; button: "Find my match >"). It is qualified and concrete - by the CTA she knows it's leak-resistant underwear for the sneeze and that the quiz finds her size and how many pairs. Meta CTA button: "Take Quiz" (or "Learn More" if Take Quiz is unavailable). Land on the live hero via a=m, utm_content=pads (a product word, not a condition word); ad name code only, e.g. V1-a_75_handbag. Do NOT say "2-minute quiz" (not timed yet).
end_card: Warm Cream card. Lowercase "leapproof" wordmark top ("leap" primary + "proof" italic Claret, Fraunces). Three stacked lines: "Not a pad, not a diaper." / "30 nights to see if they hold - money back if they don't." / Claret button "Find my match >". The folded plain black CJ brief sits small beside it. No price, no gifts, no stars, no urgency. (Money-back half added so the de-risk is visible, consistent with the landing bullet and the locked §4 wording.)
cuts: MAIN CUT (~35s, the feed/primary): beats 1-6 exactly as above - hook 0-3s (undated 'Sneeze. Little pee.' open, liner dominant frame 1), self-roast 3-11s (with the 0.4s '...or this.' brief pre-tease at ~8.5s; the silent 3-6s bridge beat is dropped and the TEASE bridge folded into the VO lead-in), reveal 11-23s, resolve+CTA 23-30s, end card 30-35s. This is the one to ship first; the hook, an early brief glimpse, the full reveal by ~11s and the CTA all land inside a 35s attention window. LONGER CUT (~55s, for longer-attention placements / A-B testing): keep beats 1-3 identical; EXTEND beat 3 with one more everyday-object liner shot (a liner peeled and binned at the end of the day) to let the routine land; ADD a care/fact beat after the reveal - on-screen 'Wash. Hang. Wear again.' with VO \"Or - wash, hang, wear it again\" over a hand rinsing and hanging the black brief (fact only; never 'wash, dry', no eco words); ADD a second everyday movement in leggings (she walks out the front door). Then the same resolve + end card. Trim rule for a 30s version: shorten the self-roast to three lines (bunches / shifts / another one in the trash) and keep the '...or this.' pre-tease; the reveal and CTA are untouched. Nothing performance-related, no laugh/sneeze/jump after the brief appears, in any cut.

compliance_check.banned_words: Clean. No incontinence, discreet, dignity, protection, accident, bladder, bladder weakness or SUI. The dated 'It's 2026' line is REMOVED (undated open 'Sneeze. Little pee.'). 'Diaper' appears ONLY as what we are NOT ('feels like a diaper' describes the liner; 'Not a diaper' is the payoff). No absolutes: no 100%/zero/never/leak-proof/stays dry. 'Hold' appears only inside the guarantee ('see if they hold / if they don't hold'). 'pee' is brand-approved (the live hero is 'I'll pee myself').
compliance_check.cj_column: CJ column respected. Enemy limited to the locked form/routine attributes: bunches, shifts, feels like a diaper, another one in the trash every day (US 'trash', not 'bin', per plan lines 649/685). 'Shifts' is supported by the quiz REACT card ('Pads bunch and shift the second you move'). The staccato read of the locked §11 enemy sentence ('Pads and liners bunch, feel like a diaper, and go in the bin every day') is flagged to Nikita for explicit sign-off (open question). The hook is REPETITION-framed ('Still packing a spare liner?'), not adequacy/wrong-tool ('still the plan' was dropped per the compliance minor). No mechanism, no Leak-Lock, no ml/oz/layers/absorbency, no 'lab-tested', no pour/spill demo, no 'built for pee not blood', no claim pads/liners 'fail' or 'can't hold', and NO attack on period underwear. The brief shown is the real CJ sample generated from the 5 reference photos, no lace.
compliance_check.meta_you_rule: Passes. No second-person condition statement. The moment line is impersonal ('Sneeze. Little pee.'); the hook question is about the routine, impersonal ('Still packing a spare liner?') - no 'you leak', 'your bladder', or 'after your baby'. The VO speaks 'pee' but never 'you'. The narrator never says 'I' or 'we'. The caption's line 2 is kept general and third-person ('A big sneeze, a little pee') per the compliance minor - never 'when you sneeze you'.
compliance_check.dramatization_label: Not required for V1-a. Every big laugh, the same panic.

Laughing too hard can mean a little pee — so there's a spare liner in her clutch, just in case. But a liner bunches, shifts, and goes in the trash every day.

There's another plan: plain black briefs. Not a pad, not a diaper. Soft, stretchy, black — you pull them on and wash them, no spare to pack.

Take the quiz and find your match. It works out your size and how many pairs you need, then 30 nights to see if they hold. Money back if they don't.
